STATE THROUGH ITS CHIEF SECRETARY  GOVERNMENT OF NCT OF DELHI .
 VERSUS  SAVITRI AGARWAL & ORS. 
 O R D E R Delay condoned.
Leave granted.
We have heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respective parties finally today.

Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order dated 18-08-2015 passed by the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in WP(C) No. 4053/2015, by which the High Court has allowed the said writ petition and has declared that with respect to the land in question, the acquisition proceedings are deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
the Government of NCT of Delhi has preferred the present appeal.

From the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court, it appears that while allowing the Writ Petition and declaring that the acquisition with respect to the land in question is deemed to have lapsed, the High Court has relied upon and considered the earlier decision of this State Through Its Chief Secretary ... vs Savitri Agarwal on 13 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64528812/
1 Court in the case of Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr. Vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki & Ors.
(2014) 3 SCC 183 by observing that the compensation has not been paid though it was the case on behalf of the appellant that the compensation was deposited in the Treasury.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute and cannot be disputed that the decision of this Court in the case of Pune Municipal Corporation (supra) has been subsequently overruled by the Constitution Bench decision of this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and Others, (2020) 8 SCC 129.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In that view of the matter, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court is unsustainable and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the matter is to be remitted to the High Court to decide the same afresh in accordance with law and on its own merits, considering the observations made by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) and/or any Contd..
- 3 - other decision(s) which may be placed before the High Court.
In view of the above and for the reasons stated hereinabove, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court is hereby quashed and set aside.

The matter is remitted to the High Court to decide and dispose of the Writ Petition afresh in accordance with law and on its own merits and in light of the decision of the Constitution Bench of this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) and/or any other decision(s) which may be placed before the High Court.
The present appeal is accordingly allowed to the aforesaid extent.
No costs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order dated 18-08-2015 passed by the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in WP(C) No. 4053/2015, by which the High Court has allowed the said writ petition and has declared that with respect to the land in question, the acquisition proceedings are deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
the Government of NCT of Delhi has preferred the present appeal.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is not in dispute and cannot be disputed that the decision of this Court in the case of Pune Municipal Corporation (supra) has been subsequently overruled by the Constitution Bench decision of this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and Others, (2020) 8 SCC 129.
In that view of the matter, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court is unsustainable and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the matter is to be remitted to the High Court to decide the same afresh in accordance with law and on its own merits, considering the observations made by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) and/or any Contd..
- 3 - other decision(s) which may be placed before the High Court.
